doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Advice to students: openness, versatility and love of music
summary: Bailey says musicians should be open to all music, able to hear and read, and love it passionately to make a living.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: What do you tell your students, I’m kind of leapfrogging to something I was going to ask later but do your students need to be versatile to make a living in this world today? How do you describe that to them?

Yeah, I mean I think — here’s what I think about it. In terms of musicianship, I mean because again, I grew up in a family with professional musicians so I never really thought much about it, but a lot of people were coming — they don’t really understand what is this path that you’re going out on. And from my point of view growing up, I wanted to get my ears together and my musicianship together. Because I was like if I can hear it I can play it, so if somebody calls me for a gig and also where I can read it, I can — that’s all I want to do is just make a living playing the guitar. And I didn’t care if it was a country band or — so I feel like that openness to music has got to be number one. And the love of music. You have to love it so passionately for those times when it’s really hard. That love has got to be there. So I think — I don’t know, you could think of maybe put it maybe more, [inaudible]. You could go out and buy the Powerball lottery ticket and maybe you’re going to win, but you could also invest your money and diversify your funds and you’ll probably be successful, a lot more successful. Maybe you’re not going to be a millionaire but you’re going to be more successful.
